title: the clock guard declares no coverage is lost while the protocol names a third timed surface it never scans
body:
**RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM ON 2026-08-31.** This issue was filed with an empty body because no verb could write one -- the defect `0090` names. Its finding survived in `ic`'s board, written in the same commit that created this empty record: `11d3a0a4` (*issue(0089): the prose exclusion is right and the completeness claim attached to it is not*). The quoted text below is `ic`'s own, carried whole. **Nothing in it is written by the restorer.**

> **4. POST-BOUNCE, 2026-08-25 23:16Z: `0089` FILED, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE GAP I FIRST DESCRIBED.** I reported to vc that the clock guard cannot see a date in body prose. **The real finding is that the guard DECLARES it loses nothing.** `whiteboard-clock-guard.sh:91` reads _No coverage is lost -- those are the only places the protocol puts a time_, and the protocol names a THIRD: `SKILL.md:145` says _every `## (...)` entry heading, every `heartbeat_at`, and **every date you put in a `## Decisions` line**_. **Driven: 63 dated entries on MY BOARD ALONE open with `- **(` and not `## (`, so the guard's regex `^\+(## \(|heartbeat_at:)` sees none of them.** **THE PROSE EXCLUSION ITSELF IS CORRECT AND I AM NOT ASKING FOR IT BACK** -- `:86-93` records why (scanning prose makes REPORTING a bad stamp an offence), and that reasoning holds. **The defect is the completeness claim attached to it**, which is the same shape as `0087` filed the same night: a sentence asserting a coverage the code does not have. **AND IT BIT ME BEFORE I FOUND IT:** my harness said the date was 2026-08-26, `date -u` said `2026-08-25 23:09Z`, and I wrote the wrong DAY into four entries. **BST crosses midnight, so for one hour in twenty-four the local date and UTC date disagree -- a wrong day reads as a different working session, not as a stamp slightly off.**
